items.title: WBD Stock Is Running. Is There Fuel Left?
items.summary: After a powerful run to new highs, this media giant's stock is asking every investor the same question: is the turnaround in streaming enough to carry the whole company higher.

items.title: Is Verizon Stock Cheap, Or Just Done Growing?
items.summary: Verizon Communications (VZ) trades at about 12 times earnings, against an S&P 500 median of 22.4. A discount that wide usually follows a collapse. Not here. The stock returned 14.1% over the past twelve months, behind the index's 17.9%, and management has raised parts of its 2026 guidance in two straight quarters. So is this a good business on sale or a fair price for a company that has stopped growing.

items.title: What Are Disney Stock Bulls Not Worried About?
items.summary: Walt Disney (DIS) owns theme parks and streaming services. The stock costs 21.8 times its earnings of the past year. The S&P 500 is at 22.6 times. So you pay less than the market for these businesses. That case only pays off if two things are both true. Disney's latest earnings call gave a reason to doubt the first. What did management say about ad prices.

items.title: How Far Can Comcast Stock Fall, And How Long Would You Wait?
items.summary: Comcast (CMCSA) trades near $22, about 29% below its 52-week high, and the market has not been falling with it. The S&P 500 returned close to 18% over the past year, while Comcast lost about 21%. The company is in the middle of a broadband pivot that it says is holding its own results down. So the question is not how hard Comcast drops in a crisis. It is how long it stays down.

items.title: Comcast (CMCSA) Stock Moves -2.22%: What You Should Know
items.summary: Comcast (CMCSA) closed at $22.42 in the latest trading session, marking a -2.22% move from the prior day.

items.title: Why Does AT&T Stock Cost Less Than A Slower-Growing Verizon?
items.summary: AT&T (T) grows faster than Verizon, yet it trades at a far lower multiple of earnings. In its five-company peer group it ranks second on growth and margin but only third on its earnings multiple. Management calls that a disparity, and it has raised its buyback to take advantage of it.

items.title: Can Paramount+ Lift Paramount Skydance Stock While The Warner Deal Sits In Court?
items.summary: Paramount Skydance (PSKY) stock is down 42% over the past year and trades about 47% below its 52-week high. Since 2010, its only rally of more than 30% inside two months came in 2025. The strongest case for another is Paramount+, where subscriber growth sped up between the first and second quarters of 2026, though management expects subscribers to stay relatively flat in the third. That case has to outlast a court fight over Warner Bros. Discovery.
